answer: A gale of cheap fake identities cannot survive a work-bonded registry: every agent must lock a refundable stake and finish a public, verifiable task before it can trade, and its record is written into a jade ledger that peers audit. Onboarding stays velvet-smooth for honest agents, but each new identity costs one full stake plus real compute. A thousand Sybils cost a thousand stakes, and any identity caught lying loses its stake to the commons, so the attack turns unprofitable before it scales.
